conditions.label: Anemia in chronic disease
conditions.note: anemia of chronic inflammation from active rheumatoid arthritis, per hematology

documents.title: Hematology Consultation Letter
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Date of service: 12/30/2024

Re: Patricia Kelleher, DOB 04/18/1968

Ms. Kelleher, 56, is seen for scheduled Felty syndrome follow-up, with your November note and CBC in hand. For the last two to three months she has felt more worn down than usual. Her mornings have changed: stiffness now lasts beyond an hour, and the small joints of both hands and the wrists swell. No fevers, infections, bleeding or weight change.

History: seropositive RA since 2014; the rheumatology synovial biopsy at diagnosis showed pannus with plasma cells and lymphocytes. Felty syndrome since 2021 (marrow hypocellular with maturation arrest; splenic aspirate benign). Glucocorticoid-related osteoporosis. Chronic fatigue syndrome. Bilateral carpal tunnel release 2016.
Medications: methotrexate 20 mg weekly; prednisone 5 mg each morning; folic acid 1 mg except methotrexate day; risedronate 35 mg weekly; calcium carbonate/vitamin D3 600 mg/400 IU twice daily; filgrastim 300 mcg SC as needed for ANC <1000.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis); ibuprofen (gastropathy).
Family history: mother RA; maternal aunt SLE; father type 2 diabetes and hypertension.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, part-time library work.

Exam: soft tissue swelling over MCPs and wrists bilaterally. Spleen palpable below the costal margin.

Data: hemoglobin 10.0 g/dL. Serum iron 38 mcg/dL (low), ferritin 140 ng/mL (normal). ESR 46 mm/h, CRP 34 mg/L. RF and anti-CCP positive. White count and ANC at her baseline.

Impression: the fall in hemoglobin fits anemia of chronic inflammation - low circulating iron with preserved stores, in the setting of increased RA activity. Inflammatory signaling sequesters iron; iron supplementation would not be expected to help. Neutropenia stable.

Recommendations: the anemia should follow control of the arthritis; I have asked her to see rheumatology promptly about the joint symptoms. No iron. Continue filgrastim as needed. CBC in 6 months.

Hematology & Oncology

documents.title: Blood doctor visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw hematology last Monday. She said the lower hemoglobin is from inflammation and not low iron, and that I need to get the arthritis calmed down. Rheumatology finally gave me Feb 4. Just letting you know since I don't think they send you things very fast. Happy new year. Pat

documents.title: RE: Blood doctor visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks Pat, this helps. I'll watch for her letter. Glad rheumatology is in early February - if the swelling gets worse before then, or you get a fever, let me know.

documents.title: Hematology Letter Received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hematology consultation from 12/30/2024 received by fax and scanned. Routed to PCP. PCP reviewed: anemia of chronic inflammation added to problem list; no iron per hematology.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u fatigue, joints, anemia.

Saw rheumatology in February. Per patient they examined her hands, kept methotrexate and prednisone the same, and will see her in the summer. No letter yet. Mornings a bit easier than in the fall, still stiff close to an hour some days. Energy poor but she is getting to her shifts.

Hematology letter (12/30) reviewed: anemia of chronic inflammation, ESR/CRP up, iron low with normal ferritin. No iron.

Exam: mild residual puffiness at MCPs, wrists not warm. Spleen tip palpable. No bruising. Lungs clear.

A/P:
- RA: per rheumatology, no change.
- Anemia of chronic disease: recheck CBC today.
- Felty/neutropenia: stable.
- Osteoporosis: risedronate, calcium/D.
Screening mammogram this spring; order placed.

reports.text: Digital breast tomosynthesis, both breasts. Compared with 11/2023 and 09/2022. Heterogeneously dense parenchyma. No mass, grouped calcifications or distortion.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Date of visit: 06/23/2025. Copy sent to PCP on request.

CC: tired, bruises on arms.

HPI: 57 yo F with seropositive RA and known Felty syndrome on methotrexate and prednisone. Weeks of persistent fatigue. Over the past several days she noticed bruises on both forearms without injury she can recall. Several colds since spring. Joint pain and morning stiffness about an hour, mainly hands and knees, longstanding. No bleeding gums, nosebleeds, melena or hematuria. No fever.

Meds: methotrexate 20 mg weekly, prednisone 5 mg daily, folic acid, risedronate, calcium/vit D, filgrastim prn.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis), ibuprofen (GI).

Exam: T 37.0 C, BP 122/76, P 74, RR 14. Comfortable. Scattered small ecchymoses on both forearms, no petechiae. Spleen mildly enlarged to palpation. Synovial thickening of both wrists; no erythema or warmth of any joint. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

Results: WBC 2.4, Hgb 11.1, plt 140. INR normal. RF positive, anti-CCP positive.

MDM: bruising and fatigue with mild cytopenias in known Felty syndrome; counts near her reported baseline, no active bleeding, afebrile. Safe for discharge.

Disposition: home. Follow up with hematology and PCP this week or next. Return for bleeding, fever, or worsening bruising.

documents.title: Went to the ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I went to the emergency room yesterday afternoon because I'm so tired and I had bruises up both arms. They did blood work and said my counts were low but not dangerous and sent me home. They told me to see you and hematology. Can I get in this week or next?

documents.title: RE: Went to the ER last night
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Glad you're home. You're booked Monday 6/30 at 2:30 with the doctor. We've requested the ER record. Please call hematology to let them know as well. Any bleeding or fever before Monday, call us right away.

documents.title: Post-ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after ED visit 6/23 for fatigue and arm bruising. ED record not yet received; patient reports counts were low and she was sent home.

Today: bruises fading, no new ones. No bleeding. Still tired. Had a run of colds this spring, each self-limited. No fevers. Morning stiffness about an hour.

Exam: afebrile. Few yellowing ecchymoses on forearms. No petechiae, no gum bleeding. Spleen palpable a little below the costal margin. Wrists thickened, not warm. Lungs clear.

A/P: Felty syndrome with low counts, likely accounting for the easy bruising. Repeat CBC today. Hematology appointment moved up to mid-July per patient. Rheumatology visit in August. Continue current medicines. Infection precautions reviewed.

documents.title: ED Record Received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: ED record 06/23/2025 received after second request. Scanned, routed to PCP. PCP reviewed - no change in plan.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, age 57.

Summer: hematology in July per patient - counts stable, filgrastim still as needed (letter not received). Rheumatology August, no medication change per patient. Bruising has not recurred. Joints calmer than last winter.

Screens: PHQ-2 1. No falls. Functional status unchanged. Proxy on file.

Exam: well. Spleen tip palpable. Hands with chronic changes, no active synovitis.

Prevention: mammogram 5/2025 negative. Pap 2027. Colonoscopy 2028. DXA 2023 stable; next one could be considered next year. Flu and COVID in October.

Labs today: CBC, CMP, vitamin D. Follow-up in winter.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu (trivalent) R deltoid and 2025-26 COVID L deltoid. Allergies reviewed. No reaction during observation.

documents.title: Lab Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hemoglobin better than last winter. ANC just above 1000. Liver and kidney fine. Copied to rheum/heme.
